Our live broadcast is about to start. If you haven't joined yet, you'd better hurry up. Today, we're going to talk about how to make shoes. We're going to make a pair of men's shoes and share the materials for this live broadcast with you. If you're interested, you can do it yourself. ## Previous Learning Reference You can refer to our previous live broadcast about self-defined writing and hair. We're going to make a pair of new shoes for your Cologne model. ## Loading the Template First of all, we're going to load our template into it. Then, we load the corresponding model into it. I made a pair of shoes like this that are from our men's model. The virtual model will also be shared with everyone. If you're interested in it, you can reply to the materials and links with the official public account of Cologne to get our related materials. ## Setting Up the Template After we load this template, I'll show you the location where this template needs to be run. I'm going to give it an open position. You can see that I'm now opening a horizontal position. Then, I'm going to give it a split line and choose the position where the board needs to be symmetrical. Using our shortcut Control + D, we will duplicate the board and the floating line to match it. ## Positioning the Boards Next, we're going to move some of the boards back to the 2D window, closer to our virtual model. We will then click on the 3D window to reset the 2D board and put our board in front of our model. ## Making the Shoe We will make the shoe this time. I will select all the other panels in addition to the bottom and side of the shoe, and then save it. I will share the live materials with you this time, as it is particularly difficult to make this shoe panel. ### Distinguishing Front and Back We open a physical surface like this to distinguish the front or back of my current panel for convenience. Using the positioning tool, I arrange the bottom of my shoe. You can see that it is in a relatively positive state. ## Adjusting Panel Size Since our panels are small, we can select all the panels first and then reduce their particle diameter to 5. The size of the panel is relatively small, and it is crucial to arrange the position of the bottom of our shoes well. ## Checking Positions We will look at its position from various angles. I will rotate it to check the position of the bottom of my shoe. After that, I will change it to the opposite side, adjusting the front position. ## Cutting the Board After adjusting the position of the bottom of my shoe, the bottom is connected to my foot, while the other side is connected to the ground. I will directly cut the outer layer of the board. The outer layer can be copied from the current board position and aligned in the same direction. ## Sewing the Shoe Next, we can delete the sewing line of the bottom of the shoe, select this board simultaneously, and remove the joint of the bottom of the shoe. We will later make some adjustments to the bottoms of the two shoes. ### Front View We turn to the front to see the effect. Next, I will sew a pair of shoes. This is the side of the bottom of the shoe, which is sewn to the back like a circle. ## Final Adjustments I have given two starting and ending points on this board. We just need to sew them according to these two points. I found that I sewed in the wrong direction on both sides, so I will correct this. ## Establishing Sewing Relationships Next, I sew the top of the shoe with the top of the board, and the bottom of the shoe with the bottom of the board. Then, we will sew the height of the side of the shoe together. ### Arranging the Pieces Since I have established a sewing relationship with the side of the shoe, I only need to select the side of the shoe in the 3D window and move these two pieces. I will add this side directly to the side, and you can see that it is arranged correctly. ## Simulation Let’s open the simulation to check its shape. You can see that this is a shoe base, which consists of three boards: a top layer, a bottom layer, and a side layer. This simulates the thickness of the real shoe. ### Adjusting the Sewing Line There's a little trick here. To improve the shape, we can change the folding angle of the sewing line from 180 degrees to 90 degrees. This will create a right-angle sewing angle for a better effect. ## Applying Fabric Next, we need to add a fabric about the bottom of the shoe. I will use the physical fabric of Trim Hardware, which we bring with us in the software. You can apply this fabric directly. ### Freezing Layers I have frozen the upper and lower layers of the shoe base, allowing us to move one side to create the effect of sticking to the foot. This side will resemble a real shoe base, with a height from the front to the back. ## Activating the Virtual Model In the next step, I will activate this virtual model so that it can conflict with our board.
